evals.name: lucky-drawio-creation
evals.prompt: Create a fun retro board for our sprint review. I feel lucky. Draw.io please.
evals.expected_output: A .drawio file with a themed retro board, autonomous theme/section choices, sticky-note pool, and facilitation widgets

assertions.text: A .drawio file is produced at the output path
The .drawio file is well-formed XML with an mxfile or mxGraphModel root
The board has a clearly-named title/theme (autonomous theme chosen since user said 'I feel lucky')
Board contains 3-6 active columns/sections including an Action Items section
Each active column has visible space for at least 10 sticky notes
At least one theme-native sentiment or diagnostic widget is present (mood, energy, confidence, etc.)
A copy/paste pool of blank sticky notes in multiple colors is included
Dot-voting tokens or markers are included
Sticky notes are editable Draw.io cell objects (not baked into a background image)
Wording is blame-free and process-focused

evals.name: serious-mermaid-incident
evals.prompt: Make a Mermaid retrospective board for a production outage post-mortem we're running tomorrow with 8 engineers. Keep it serious and blame-free, focus on timeline + prevention experiments.
evals.expected_output: A Mermaid diagram suitable for incident retro: timeline, what helped, what hurt, prevention, action items; serious tone; no theming clutter

assertions.text: Output contains a Mermaid diagram (in a ```mermaid block or a .mmd/.md file)
Mermaid syntax is valid and parses without errors
Diagram includes a timeline / facts node or section
Diagram includes a 'what helped' or 'what worked' section
Diagram includes a 'what hurt recovery' or 'pain' section
Diagram includes a prevention experiments section
Diagram includes an action items section referencing owner and due date
Tone is serious and blame-free — no words like 'fault', 'blame', 'who caused'
Dense board is split into overview + action-item table when needed, OR stays compact and readable
Includes facilitation guidance (timeboxes, session goal, or owner/due-date prompts) in notes

evals.name: post-retro-confluence-jira
evals.prompt:
Here are sticky notes from yesterday's retro (text-only, dot votes in parens):
Went well: 'Pairing on auth refactor' (5), 'Faster CI after caching' (3), 'Demo to stakeholders nailed it' (2)
Did not go well: 'Standups running 25+ min' (6), 'Flaky e2e tests on main' (4), 'PR reviews stalled 2+ days' (4)
Ideas: 'Round-robin standup facilitator' (3), 'Quarantine flaky test suite' (5)
Please summarize into Confluence notes and Jira action drafts.
evals.expected_output: Confluence-ready summary with themes/decisions; Jira action drafts with title, description, owner placeholder, due date, acceptance criteria

assertions.text: A confluence.md (or equivalent) file is produced
A jira.md (or equivalent) file is produced
Confluence notes contain Summary, Themes, Decisions, and Action items sections
Top-voted pain point ('Standups running 25+ min', 6 votes) is reflected as a top theme or action
Top-voted idea ('Quarantine flaky test suite', 5 votes) is reflected as an action or experiment
Each Jira draft includes a Title field
Each Jira draft includes a Description field
Each Jira draft includes an Owner (or Owner placeholder) field
Each Jira draft includes a Due date (or Due date placeholder) field
Each Jira draft includes Acceptance criteria
Action items are written in experiment format or are specific, owned, and measurable
Wording is blame-free and process-focused
